$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/ioctl.h> (POSIX) — c16 (SQLite os_unix) + TF-C92 (the request-ENCODING macros). SQLite calls ioctl in a few places (e.g. F2FS / proxy-locking paths). Verified against glibc misc/sys/ioctl.h + xnu/bsd/sys/ioctl.h: the prototype `int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, ...)` is IDENTICAL on glibc and Darwin — variadic, the request arg is `unsigned long` (u64 on LP64) on both → a flat variadic signature `fn(i32, u64, ...) -> i32` (the c14c variadic-extern path). Gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho]. | ★ TF-C92 CORRECTION — the pre-c92 comment here asserted 'the _IOC/_IOR/_IOW request-ENCODING macros differ per-OS, but SQLite doesn't use this header's macros, so none are shipped (no over-ship)'. The second clause was FALSE and it cost a whole TU. SQLite uses them at TWO MEASURED sites: (1) macho — sqlite/src/os_unix.c:2986 `#define afpfsByteRangeLock2FSCTL _IOWR('z', 23, struct ByteRangeLockPB2)`, live under the os_unix.c:2966 guard `#if defined(__APPLE__) && SQLITE_ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE` (`__APPLE__` is a macho-gated DSS predefine and LOCKING_STYLE self-defaults to 1 on Apple at os_unix.c:66-70), the tag declared at os_unix.c:2976 and the macro consumed at os_unix.c:3013 `err = fsctl(path, afpfsByteRangeLock2FSCTL, &pb, 0);`; (2) elf — os_unix.c:392-396, `_IO(F2FS_IOCTL_MAGIC, 1|2|3|5)` ×4 plus `_IOR(F2FS_IOCTL_MAGIC, 12, u32)` under `#ifdef __linux__`. An angle `#include` resolves to DESCRIPTORS ONLY (the real <sys/ioccom.h> / <asm-generic/ioctl.h> TEXT is never read), so with no descriptor row `_IOWR` survived to the parser as a CALL whose 3rd argument is a type-name — `struct` cannot start an expression → `error[P0009] … got 'struct'` at os_unix.c:2986:56, MEASURED as the sole diagnostic in that TU (a parse death, hence a FLOOR: it aborts before semantic analysis). | ENCODINGS, both MEASURED from a real header ON DISK, then differentially re-verified by compiling each replacement string beside the genuine macro. macho ← /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/sys/ioccom.h: IOCPARM_MASK 0x1fff, IOC_VOID 0x20000000, IOC_OUT 0x40000000, IOC_IN 0x80000000, IOC_INOUT (IN|OUT) 0xc0000000, `_IOC(inout,group,num,len) (inout | ((len & IOCPARM_MASK) << 16) | ((group) << 8) | (num))`. elf ← musl arch/generic/bits/ioctl.h (the Linux asm-generic ABI, verbatim on this machine under the emsdk sysroot): `_IOC(a,b,c,d) (((a)<<30) | ((b)<<8) | (c) | ((d)<<16))` with _IOC_NONE 0U / _IOC_WRITE 1U / _IOC_READ 2U, i.e. DIR at bit 30 (2-bit field), SIZE at 16, TYPE at 8, NR at 0 — so _IOWR's dir is 3u (READ|WRITE), NOT a single bit as on Darwin. The two OSes disagree on the DIRECTION FIELD ENTIRELY (Darwin: one bit each at 29/30/31, VOID has its own bit; Linux: a 2-bit code at 30, NONE=0) — this is exactly the per-OS divergence that belongs in `when:{format}` rows and NOWHERE else. Cross-checks: macho `_IOWR('z',23,struct ByteRangeLockPB2)` = 0xc0207a17 (sizeof 32 → 0x20<<16, 'z'=0x7a<<8, 23) — byte-identical to the SDK macro; elf `_IOR(0xf5,12,u32)` = 0x8004f50c and `_IO(0xf5,1..5)` = 0xf501/f502/f503/f505 — the published Linux F2FS_IOC_* numbers, which is an INDEPENDENT witness that the musl formula was transcribed correctly. | ★ THE DIRECTION BITS ARE UNSIGNED (`0x…u` / `0u`/`1u`/`2u`/`3u`) — interop-critical, and MEASURED rather than assumed, because the two halves of that claim are not equally true. Darwin spells them `(__uint32_t)0x…` and musl spells them `0U/1U/2U` for one reason: the result widens to the `unsigned long` request parameter of ioctl/fsctl, and a SIGNED top-bit value that sign-extends passes a WRONG REQUEST NUMBER — a silent wrong-value miscompile at the syscall boundary, never a diagnostic. On the MACHO arms the `u` is EXPLICITNESS, not a repair: `0xc0000000` already has type `unsigned int` by C 6.4.4.1p5 (it does not fit in `int`), and DSS + clang were measured to agree on `(unsigned long)0xc0000000 == 0xc0000000`. On the ELF arms it is genuinely LOAD-BEARING: `2 << 30` OVERFLOWS a signed int, and the two compilers DIVERGE on that UB — clang widens the fold to 0xffffffff80000000, DSS widens it to 0x80000000 — so a signed spelling would make DSS compute an ioctl number that disagrees with every native consumer of the same header, while `2u << 30` makes them agree. Hence the suffix on EVERY arm: it removes the question instead of resting on a per-compiler UB choice or on the escalation rule happening to rescue the Darwin case. `examples/c/shipped_ioctl_iowr_macho/` pins the exact encoded values with `_Static_assert` (plus a forward guard that the widening never sign-extends), so a shift/mask/direction regression is RED at compile time rather than a bad ioctl at runtime; MEASURED reds: deleting the `_IOWR` row restores P0009 at os_unix.c:2986:56, deleting only its macho VARIANT does the same (so variant SELECTION is pinned too), and giving macho `_IOR` the elf direction code fails the value assert loud. | FAMILY COMPLETENESS — a real tension, recorded not resolved-in-silence. TF-C90's lesson says descriptor COMPLETENESS is a correctness requirement, because a winning descriptor SHADOWS the real header that would have carried the missing names; here the shadowing is TOTAL (the header text is never read), so this descriptor is the ONLY source of these names, and a `#if defined(_IOW)` probe turns an under-shipped family into a SILENTLY-WRONG BRANCH rather than a loud absence. The no-over-ship rule pulls the other way: every unexercised row is a claim no test checks, and an untested claim is how the false comment above survived. RESOLUTION: ship the CLOSED, PORTABLE set of four — `_IO`/`_IOR`/`_IOW`/`_IOWR` — identical in name, arity and meaning on both shipped OSes, every one MEASURED from a real header and every one value-pinned by tests/ffi + the corpus example (so completeness costs no unverified surface). `_IOW` and macho `_IOR`/`_IO` exceed the corpus's current demand DELIBERATELY: they are the same one formula the corpus rows already prove, differing only in the direction constant. DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: `_IOC` and the direction-bit vocabulary (`IOC_VOID`/`IOC_OUT`/`IOC_IN`/`IOC_INOUT`/`IOCPARM_MASK` on Darwin, `_IOC_NONE`/`_IOC_WRITE`/`_IOC_READ` on Linux). Those are the IMPLEMENTATION vocabulary, not a portable interface — the two OSes disagree on both the spellings and the bit layout, so `_IOC` is unusable without also shipping per-OS names that no corpus site references (verified: zero hits for IOC_*/IOCPARM_*/_IOC_* across sqlite src/ + ext/) and whose mere availability would invite a portability bug. Their absence is LOUD, not silent: `_IOC(...)`/`IOC_OUT` reach the parser as an undeclared function/identifier → S0001. Each of the four rows therefore INLINES its numerics and is self-contained — no `constants` surface, and no macro body that depends on another descriptor macro expanding inside it. | ★ THE ONE HAZARD THE ENUMERATION ABOVE OMITTED — the SIZE FIELD WAS UNBOUNDED in both arms, and each one overflowed DIFFERENTLY and SILENTLY. macho MASKS (`sizeof(t) & 0x1fffu`, verbatim from the SDK's IOCPARM_MASK 0x1fff at sys/ioccom.h:74), so a type LARGER than 8191 bytes WOULD be truncated to its low 13 bits — an 8192-byte type encoding size 0, i.e. an ioctl number that is well-formed, wrong, and diagnostic-free. elf does NOT mask (`sizeof(t) << 16`, verbatim from the musl `_IOC`), so the field just KEPT growing: at `sizeof(t) >= 0x4000` bit 30 lights up and the value collides with the 2-bit DIRECTION field — a 0x4000-byte `_IOR` encoding as 0x80000000|0x40000000, which IS `_IOWR`, so the kernel would copy the argument the WRONG WAY. ⚠ READ THOSE TWO SENTENCES AS THE ARITHMETIC OF THE BARE FORMULA, NOT AS DSS'S BEHAVIOUR TODAY: the ceiling recorded below makes both of those types UNCOMPILABLE, so neither number can be reached. Both arms faithfully reproduced their source header, and NEITHER USERSPACE HEADER GUARDS THIS. MEASURED on this machine — `grep -r _IOC_TYPECHECK` over the emsdk musl sysroot returns ZERO hits, and Darwin sys/ioccom.h carries no compile-time check. The guard that exists is KERNEL-INTERNAL: Linux include/uapi/asm-generic/ioctl.h defines `_IOC_TYPECHECK(t)` as `(sizeof(t) == sizeof(t[1]) && sizeof(t) < (1 << _IOC_SIZEBITS)) ? sizeof(t) : __invalid_size_argument_for_IOC` — a deliberate compile/link error — only under `#ifdef __KERNEL__`, while the userspace `#else` arm is a bare `sizeof(t)`. | ★★ CLOSED BY [[D-FFI-IOCTL-SIZE-FIELD-OVERFLOW-SILENT]] — AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE, WHICH DESCRIBED THIS DEFECT IN FULL AND THEN DECLINED TO FILE IT ON THE GROUND THAT `a ceiling is a mechanism and not a row`, WAS WRONG TO. Each SIZED arm now ends with `(0u * sizeof(struct { char dss_ioctl_arg_size_exceeds_<CEILING>[(sizeof(t) > <mask>u) ? -1 : 1]; }))`: a NAMED array MEMBER whose length is 1 in range and -1 over it, so an oversized type is a C 6.7.6.2p1 constraint violation at COMPILE time and the array's NAME is what gcc, clang and mingw-w64 gcc print (MSVC names neither shape; DSS carries the identifier in its raw source slice — the five-way measurement is in (2) below). macho refuses `sizeof(t) > 0x1fffu` (Darwin IOCPARM_MASK, 8191); elf refuses `sizeof(t) > 0x3fffu` (Linux _IOC_SIZEMASK, 16383 — the same predicate the kernel spells `sizeof(t) < (1 << _IOC_SIZEBITS)`). `_IO` has no size operand on either format and is untouched. AGNOSTIC BY CONSTRUCTION: both ceilings live in the `when:{format}` arms that already existed, so no engine branch is involved — and the SAME 8192-byte type is ACCEPTED on elf and REFUSED on macho, a property no single global ceiling could have, which is what tests/ffi/test_shipped_ioctl_size_ceiling.cpp pins. THE ENCODED VALUE IS PROVABLY UNCHANGED for every accepted type: the guard is multiplied by `0u`, so its contribution is zero BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by an assumption about the struct's size, and the expression's TYPE stays `size_t` exactly as it already was (`sizeof(t) & 0x1fffu` / `sizeof(t) << 16` had already widened it). | ★★ THE SHAPE WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, AND THE TWO OBVIOUS CANDIDATES WERE MEASURED AND REJECTED. (1) The kernel's own `BUILD_BUG_ON_ZERO(e)` ≡ `(sizeof(struct { int : (-!!(e)); }))` — gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and DSS all diagnose the negative ANONYMOUS width, but MSVC 19.51.36252 COMPILES IT rc=0 (it accepts a negative anonymous bit-field width in silence) and ALSO gives the members-less struct a NON-ZERO size, so on that reference the idiom would both fail to fire and corrupt the number. A guard whose whole purpose is to delete a silent wrong value must not itself be silent on a reference. (2) The strictly-ISO `(sizeof(char[(e) ? -1 : 1]) - 1u)` — all four references accept it under the ceiling and refuse it loudly over, and on 2026-09-02 DSS's own parser refused the construct outright (`sizeof(char[4])` / `sizeof(struct T[2])` → `P_NoAlternativeMatched … got 'char'` / `got 'struct'`), so the array went on a MEMBER, where DSS already parsed it. ⚠⚠ **THAT FORCING CONSTRAINT WAS RETIRED THE SAME DAY AND THIS PARAGRAPH NO LONGER RESTS ON IT — THE SHAPE IS A MEASURED CHOICE, NOT A WORKAROUND.** [[D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-ARRAY-TYPE-NAME]] closed in the same cycle: `abstractDirectDeclarator` regained its bare `arrayDeclSuffix` arm, and every array abstract type-name parses. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-09-02 THROUGH THIS VERY DESCRIPTOR — `src/dss-config` copied outside the repo, `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` aimed at the copy, the six sized arms rewritten to the plain form — DSS compiles the plain guard AT the ceiling rc=0 and refuses ceiling+1 with the same `S_ArrayLengthOutOfRange`. So the plain form is a LIVE option today, and it was measured and REJECTED ON MERIT. ★★ **THE REASON IS THE DIAGNOSTIC, NOT THE PARSER: AN ABSTRACT DECLARATOR HAS NO IDENTIFIER (C 6.7.7p1), so the plain form cannot name what blew up — and the NAME is the entire announcement.** Five compilers, each invoked separately, at ceiling+1, MEMBER form vs PLAIN form: gcc 13.3.0 `size of array 'dss_ioctl_arg_size_exceeds_IOCPARM_MASK_8191' is negative` vs `size of unnamed array is negative`; clang 18.1.3 `'dss_ioctl_arg_size_exceeds_…' declared as an array with a negative size` vs `array size is negative`; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 as gcc; MSVC 19.51 `C2118 negative subscript` for BOTH, naming neither. THREE OF FOUR REFERENCES PRINT THE NAME. DSS's own refusal through this descriptor carries the identifier too, and the plain form's carries nothing self-describing at all — which weighs MORE here than on any reference, because DSS still mislocates a macro-expanded constraint violation to a synthetic define block and renders a raw source slice, so that identifier is the ONLY token in the whole message that says WHICH limit was exceeded. Dropping it buys a shorter line and spends the entire signal. ⚠ **THE COST OF THE CHOSEN SHAPE, RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED: MSVC emits `warning C4116: unnamed type definition in parentheses` once per USE — including every legitimate under-ceiling one — where the plain form is silent.** That is an informational warning about a legal C idiom, on a reference consulted here for ACCEPT-vs-REFUSE (which it gets right in both shapes and both directions) and which never compiles this file; it does not outweigh a named refusal. (3) A third candidate had BOTH properties and still lost: a named array as a PARAMETER of a function-pointer type-name, `(0u * sizeof(int (*)(char <the same name>[(e) ? -1 : 1])))`, names the array on the same three references AND drops C4116 — rejected because a function-pointer type inside an ioctl request encoding is markedly harder to read than a struct member, and the readability of shipped config is worth more than an informational warning on a compiler that never reads it. The chosen shape is unanimous in BOTH directions — under the ceiling DSS rc=0 and gcc/clang/mingw-w64 gcc are `-pedantic -Wall` clean; over it DSS emits S_ArrayLengthOutOfRange (carrying the C 6.7.6.2p1 citation), gcc `size of array '…' is negative`, clang `'…' declared as an array with a negative size`, MSVC `C2118 negative subscript`. | ⚠ DSS IS DELIBERATELY ABOVE ITS SOURCE HEADERS HERE. Reproducing a header faithfully governs what a name MEANS; it is not a licence to reproduce a silent wrong value. Every representable type still encodes byte-identically to the native header, and the only programs whose behaviour changed are the ones that would have computed a wrong ioctl number — on macho a truncation to the low 13 bits, on elf a size that lights bit 30 and turns an `_IOR` into an `_IOWR`, i.e. the kernel copying the argument the wrong way. NOT TRIGGERED BY THE CORPUS: every sqlite use is small — `struct ByteRangeLockPB2` 32 bytes, `u32` 4, `_IO` 0 — so the ceiling moves no shipped site, which is exactly why the boundary types live in a test rather than in the corpus. | ARCH CAVEAT (elf): the asm-generic direction layout is Linux's DEFAULT, and a few architectures override it (ppc/alpha/mips/sparc use NONE=1/READ=2/WRITE=4 with a different size field). DSS's elf targets are x86_64 + arm64, both asm-generic, so `when:{format:elf}` is exact for every target that ships today. It is NOT extensible to such an arch: a macro variant's `when` is FORMAT-ONLY by construction (src/ffi/shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp — arch is not threaded into the preprocessor), so an elf/ppc64 target would need that selector widened rather than another row here.
